name: Kara Jackson
label: September Recordings
lede: A teenage slam poet from Oak Park who got named the nation's youth poet laureate, then made a folk record that asks the question most folk records dodge.

eras.title: Oak Park, pages first
eras.text: Jackson grew up in Oak Park, Illinois, and came up through Chicago's youth poetry scene before she ever released a song. Her first audience was a slam stage, and a best friend who wanted to start a band.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does · Smith College: Music To Love
years.h: Her best friend, Maya-Gabrielle Gary, dies
years.p: The two had bonded over the Beatles and a classic rock Tumblr, and dreamed of a band. Gary died in 2016 of a rare muscle cancer.
years.xp:
Jackson told The Line of Best Fit that Gary downplayed her illness when she first mentioned it, and that she didn't grasp how serious it was. Her favourite Beatle was George, Gary's was John.

Smith College later described the debut album as honoring a high school friend lost to cancer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kara Jackson · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does
years.p: Jackson, then an Oak Park River Forest High School student, performed at the Louder Than a Bomb finals and won the Literary Award chosen by poet Patricia Smith.
years.xp: Smith praised her chapbook Bloodstone Cowboy in her citation, saying Jackson "plucks at a tangled lineage" and "brashly personifies virginity and moonshine."

years.src: Wikipedia: Kara Jackson · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does
years.h: Kara Jackson becomes U.S. National Youth Poet Laureate
years.p: She was the third to hold the title, chosen after submitting an essay on poetry and democracy. Bloodstone Cowboy came out from Haymarket Books the same year.
years.xp: Her poems had run in Poetry, Rookie and Nimrod before the laureateship. Her mother works for a labour union, and Jackson has said she grew up on protest songs.

eras.title: From page to guitar
eras.text: The poet picked up a guitar and a banjo. A small EP, a pandemic bedroom and three Chicago friends turned into an album.

years.h: A Song for Every Chamber of the Heart EP
years.p: Her first music: folk songs from a poet better known, at that point, for her chapbook.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson is on the rise · Smith College: Music To Love
years.h: Lockdown demos in her childhood bedroom
years.p: Jackson started recording the album's songs in her parents' Oak Park house during early COVID lockdowns.
years.xp: Kaina Castillo, Sen Morimoto and Nnamdi Ogbonnaya, all Chicago musicians, later rejoined her to re-record the material for the final version. She has said some songs took years to finish, and that "brain" is among the oldest.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?
years.h: "no fun/party" is her first new music in three years
years.p: The single arrived after the 2019 EP and set up the album. Jackson co-wrote it with her three producers.

eras.title: The question mark
eras.text: September Recordings put out the debut in April, and by December it was on year-end lists from Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and The Guardian.

years.src: BroadwayWorld: Kara Jackson Releases New Songs Dickhead Blues/Brain
years.h: "dickhead blues" and "brain" arrive as a double single
years.p: Jackson put out the pair three months before the album, with a lyric video for "dickhead blues".

years.src: Stereogum: Kara Jackson Announces Debut Album
years.p: Stereogum ran the first look at the record's title and release date alongside the song. The producers were Nnamdi, Kaina and Sen Morimoto.

years.src: Album of the Year: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson is on the rise
years.h: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · September Recordings
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.2, named it Best New Music and ranked it No. 19 of 2023. It's 13 songs in 52 minutes, with a question for a title and no answer attached.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Mary Retta called it a "brutally honest debut" that bends folk to Jackson's will, and wrote that many songs are "harsh and disorienting, probing and uncomfortable." On Metacritic it holds a 90 from four reviews.

Jackson has said the title's question is not one the album tries to answer. Every song is co-written by the four producers except "pawnshop," which Jackson wrote with Castillo and Morimoto.
play: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?

years.h: She graduates from Smith College, then opens for Corinne Bailey Rae
years.p: Jackson finished an English degree in 2023 and supported Bailey Rae's Black Rainbows tour.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does · Wikipedia: Kara Jackson
years.h: The Line of Best Fit names it album of the year
years.p: The same record also made year-end lists at Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and The Guardian.

eras.title: Home stage, bigger rooms
eras.text: Jackson took the album to Europe's festivals, came home to play Chicago, and then started turning up on other people's records.

years.src: Vocalo: For Kara Jackson, Pitchfork Fest is a family affair
years.h: Pitchfork Music Festival: a Chicago homecoming
years.p: Her first Pitchfork set, on the Green Stage at 2:30 p.m., with her parents in the crowd and collaborators on stage.
years.xp: She had already played Glastonbury, Roskilde and Brosella. Jackson told Vocalo the festival was "a family affair," and that opening for her childhood hero Corinne Bailey Rae felt like pausing in real time.

years.p: The track is on the band's ninth album, The Mountain. In May she appeared on the lead single for the Is God Is film companion album.
